name: The London EDITION
insider_take: Where Ian Schrager's legendary design genius meets London's coolest neighborhood – this is hospitality as art form.
whats_special: The London EDITION occupies a stunning 1908 Edwardian Baroque building that once housed the headquarters of the Berners Hotel. Designed by hospitality visionary Ian Schrager, this boutique gem features the city's most talked-about lobby restaurant, Berners Tavern, with its breathtaking collection of gilt-framed paintings covering every inch of the soaring walls. The hotel's Punch Room serves some of London's most innovative cocktails in an intimate, speakeasy-style setting.
pro_tip: Book dinner at Berners Tavern even if you're not staying – it's consistently rated among London's most Instagram-worthy dining rooms, but arrive early to admire the art collection before the dinner rush.
dont_miss: The hotel sits perfectly positioned between Oxford Street's shopping mecca and Fitzrovia's trendy galleries. You're a 3-minute walk from the BBC Broadcasting House and steps from Charlotte Street's renowned restaurant scene. The nearby Fitzroy Square, one of London's finest Georgian squares, offers a peaceful escape from the city buzz.
pros: Prime Fitzrovia location with excellent connectivity to Oxford Street and Tottenham Court Road
Sophisticated Ian Schrager design with contemporary luxury aesthetic
Award-winning BERNERS TAVERN restaurant with striking dining room design
Comprehensive wellness facilities including fitness center and spa services
cons: Premium pricing reflecting luxury positioning and central location
Contemporary minimalist design may feel stark for traditional luxury preferences
